title: The Glass Garden
text: Flowers of coloured glass grow in neat rows, roses and lilies and tulips, chiming softly in the wind. Someone tends them. The paths are swept, the beds are weeded, and shards of a broken rose lie in a careful little pile, as if waiting to be buried.

options.label: Pick a glass rose. The garden has so many.

outcomes.text: It never wilts and never breaks. When no one is near, it chimes.
The gardener comes, unhappy about its rose. It has been gardening a long time.

options.label: The wisest sweeps a path, as a guest should, and thanks the gardener for the visit.

outcomes.text: The flowers chime a little tune. The way out is shorter than the way in.

options.label: Walk carefully round the beds, and touch nothing at all.

outcomes.text: You touch not one petal. Behind you, the garden seems to relax.
